With the help of USAID's democracy office, this model was implemented in many other countries to topple governments: Georgia's "Rose Revolution" in 2003, Ukraine's "Orange Revolution" in 2004, and many more.

SIX JOURS APRÈS LES FAITS, AUCUNE AUTOPSIE N’A ENCORE ÉTÉ RÉALISÉE 😨

👉 ENFIN DES NOUVELLES DU MANIFESTANT DÉCÉDÉ LE 17 OCTOBRE À PARIS

Après PLUSIEURS JOURS SANS EXPLICATIONS CLAIRES SUR SON DÉCÈS, de NOUVELLES INFORMATIONS ont été révélées.

Il s’agit de Christophe M., 59 ans, intermittent du spectacle, qui vivait à Ivry-sur-Seine, dans le Val-de-Marne. Il était venu manifester pour le pouvoir d’achat.

Le 17 octobre, vers 18h21, les pompiers ont été alertés de la présence d’un homme inconscient près de la station de métro Jacques Bonsergent, à quelques centaines de mètres de la place de la République.

Christophe M. a été pris en charge par les secours, puis transporté à la caserne des pompiers de la rue du Château-d’Eau, où il est décédé à 18h56 d’un arrêt cardiorespiratoire, soit 35 minutes après sa prise en charge.

La préfecture de police justifie ce déplacement par les "conditions de sécurité dégradées aux alentours". Au même moment, des pillages, des barricades en feu et des tirs de gaz lacrymogènes avaient lieu dans le secteur.

👉 Sa famille prépare désormais une plainte devant l’IGPN pour "VIOLENCES VOLONTAIRES AYANT ENTRAÎNÉ LA MORT SANS INTENTION DE LA DONNER".

"Il n’avait pas de problème de santé, il n’avait pas de maladie particulière", assure son avocat.

Ses proches soupçonnent notamment l’utilisation importante de gaz lacrymogènes par les forces de l’ordre d’avoir joué un rôle dans son décès.

Sa conjointe, qui avait tenté à plusieurs reprises de le joindre sur son téléphone sans obtenir de réponse, a finalement appris son décès vers 20 heures, lorsqu’un pompier a décroché et lui a annoncé la mort de son compagnon.

SIX JOURS APRÈS LES FAITS, AUCUNE AUTOPSIE N’A ENCORE ÉTÉ RÉALISÉE, selon BFMTV. L’avocat de la famille suspecte les autorités de "JOUER LA MONTRE" et dénonce le manque de transparence de l’enquête.

"Quatre jours après sa mort, on n’a toujours aucune information", déplore-t-il. Selon lui, le parquet n’a jamais contacté sa conjointe. Seul un enquêteur, qu’il décrit comme "très froid et très distant", l’aurait appelée.

items.tx:
In December 1958 the Polish embassy in Beijing refused to let the sparrow killers onto its grounds, so the Chinese surrounded it with drummers and kept the drums going for two days until every bird sheltering in the garden had dropped dead from the air, and the diplomats cleared them up with shovels.

That is how thorough it was. The campaign had been running since the spring. Every village, school and factory was turned out with gongs, pans and firecrackers to keep the sparrows flying until their hearts gave out. Nests were torn from eaves, eggs smashed, chicks killed, and children went through the fields with slingshots and were paid by the bird. The dead came in by the basket, strung on wires, piled on carts, and the totals went up the chain as a harvest. Something close to two billion sparrows in two years. The embassy garden was the last place in the capital with birdsong in it, and the drums got that too.

A zoologist called Zhu Xi had told them before it started that a king had tried this and lost. Frederick the Great of Prussia had put a bounty on sparrows in the 1740s to save his grain and his cherries, and the sparrows went, and the caterpillars they had been eating stripped his orchards to the stalk, and the king cancelled the bounty and paid to have sparrows brought back from neighbouring states and let loose. The whole episode was in the library. The ministry had a figure for what a sparrow ate and no figure for what it did, and a man with the second figure was told to sit down.

The locusts arrived on schedule. Then the grain borers. A sparrow takes a few grains from a field in autumn and feeds its chicks nothing but insects all spring, and with the sparrows gone the insects had the rice and the wheat to themselves. The counties with the most sparrows to lose saw their grain fall the furthest, and the rice and wheat that had been holding the country up went down together.

That was 1959, and the state took its grain quota anyway, on the harvest that had been reported. What was left in the villages was not enough, and the famine that followed over the next three years is the largest in human history: tens of millions dead, the estimates running from fifteen million to forty-five, whole counties in Anhui and Sichuan where the living could not bury the dead. The sparrows were one cause among several and the economists who have gone back to the county records put the bird's share at something over two million people, with another four hundred thousand never born. Two million, from a campaign against a thing that weighs an ounce.

By 1960 the ornithologist Tso-hsin Cheng, who had been cutting open dead sparrows and counting the insects in their stomachs, got the bird struck off the list and bed bugs put in its place. There were almost no sparrows left in China to pardon. So the government did what Prussia had done two centuries before: it bought a quarter of a million sparrows from the Soviet Union and shipped them east in crates, to be released into a country that had drummed every one of their relatives out of the sky.

The animal that does the invisible job is always the one on the ledger as a cost. Take the sheep off a chalk down and the orchids are under scrub in twenty years. Fence the cattle off a Welsh hill and the bracken takes it. Empty a savannah of its herds and the grass goes to fire. All of it written down, all of it in the library, all of it available to the next committee with a figure for what a cow eats.

Beijing paid Moscow for the birds in hard currency. The men who had said so in 1958 were still not allowed to say so in 1960.

BREAKING: Catherine Herridge just dropped a bombshell that could change everything about the Ilhan Omar case...and it has nothing to do with what federal agents were looking for in Monday's raid.

Herridge is reporting that seasoned federal investigators see passport fraud as another potential avenue for criminal prosecution.

The statute at the center of it: 18 U.S.C. § 1542 — False Statement in Application. It prohibits making false statements on a passport application, using a passport obtained through false statements, or using a passport under an assumed or false name to hide criminal behavior.

And here's the part that should worry Omar's legal team: the 10-year statute of limitations on passport fraud resets every single time the individual renews their passport — if the underlying application records, such as a Social Security Number, were obtained through fraud.

So why does that matter here? Remember the birthdate change. Omar's staff had her publicly listed birth year changed from 1981 to 1982 back in May 2019. If someone lied about their true date and place of birth to obtain a Social Security Number, that fraud doesn't expire the way most people think it does. Every passport renewal restarts the clock.

And federal investigators have run this exact playbook before.

After 9/11, when the Joint Terrorism Task Force investigated Anwar al-Awlaki — the American-born cleric who became a top al Qaeda leader — a seasoned investigator ran down a scholarship scam: Awlaki had used his Yemeni passport and false claims about his birthplace to secure roughly $20,000 in USAID tuition money for Colorado State University. But the statute of limitations on the tuition fraud had already run out.

So a State Department Diplomatic Security agent found another way in. Awlaki had made false statements to secure a J-1 visa, then used a fraudulently obtained Social Security Number — falsely claiming he was born in Yemen — to obtain a U.S. passport. The passport fraud became the holding charge. Every renewal reset the 10-year clock.

Herridge's reporting doesn't say charges are coming. But it lays out a roadmap that federal investigators have walked before, and successfully.

This intervention formed part of the Greater Aba Road Infrastructure Restoration Programme under the Abia State Integrated Infrastructure Development Programme (ABSIIDP), supported by partners including the African Development Bank, Islamic Development Bank, and Canadian Climate Fund. 

I stated that in 24 months or less, these projects would be completed, ending decades of untold hardship for residents and businesses. Aba would once again thrive as the heartbeat of commerce and industry in our region. 

I sincerely appreciate our supporters, well-wishers, and residents who trooped out en masse to grace the flag-off ceremony. Your presence and encouragement reaffirmed our collective commitment to rebuilding Aba and restoring its pride of place. 

I urged all residents and business owners along these corridors to cooperate with the contractors, fulfil their civic obligations, and support this transformation. Like the phoenix rising from the ashes, our beloved Enyimba City, is coming alive again.
